Senses.PreferredTarget: the old woman burns the hermitage
AlternateTargets: the old woman's burning of the hermitage
Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘the old woman burns the hermitage.’ The phrase occurs 75 times in 34 allowlisted texts as the title of a public case. In its repeated narrative, an old woman supports a hermitage-dweller for twenty years and sends a young woman to attend him. The young woman embraces him and asks, ‘at just such a time, how is it?’ He answers, ‘a withered tree leans against a cold cliff; through the three winter months there is no warmth.’ On hearing the report, the old woman says that for twenty years she has supported only a common fellow, drives him out, and burns the hermitage. Later masters cite, verse, question, and re-appraise the case: one asks why various quarters support the monk; another proposes that the hermitage-dweller should have laughed when approached; another says that to uphold the school and establish the teaching requires such a person, speaking of the old woman. These opposed recorded appraisals belong to the case's reception; this entry does not decide between them.
Senses.Note: Zen bends a domestic act of arson into a named case continually reopened in public comment and questioning. The label names the whole encounter, not only the final fire. The usual graph for ‘hermitage’ (庵) and its witness variant (菴) spell the same word. Cross-checking ‘a withered tree leans against a cold cliff’ (枯木倚寒巖) and ‘through the three winter months there is no warmth’ (三冬無暖氣) confirms the quoted hermitage-dweller's response without turning that response into a second sense of the case title.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉婆子燒庵話，師曰：大凡扶宗立教，須是其人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later master raises ‘the old woman burns the hermitage’ case and begins: ‘generally, to uphold the school and establish the teaching requires such a person.’

Occurrences.Kwic: 龍門問：「婆子燒庵話，謂諸方扶起這僧，是何眼目？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Longmen asks: ‘In the old-woman-burns-the-hermitage case, on what discernment do various quarters support this monk?’

Occurrences.Kwic: 婆子燒庵。拈云：「這婆子俗氣不除，宛擬大人之作，當時庵主早辯來機，未免呵呵大笑。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later comment says the old woman had not shed ordinary airs and proposes that the hermitage-dweller should have recognized the approach and laughed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 婆子燒庵撲面來時無一物，明眼衲僧莫輕忽。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse headed by the case says: ‘when it comes straight at the face there is not one thing; clear-eyed patched-robed monks, do not take it lightly.’ The verse is reported without adopting it as a definition.
